sections.title: Sec 1: The Mystery of the Missing Piece
lecture_lines: What happens if we cut them?
animations: Animation step 1: Fade in a triangle with vertices labeled A, B, C. Color angle A Red (#FF5733), B Blue (#33A1FF), C Green (#33FF57).
Animation step 2: Highlight the three angles with a pulsing glow effect to emphasize their existence.
Animation step 3: Animate 'cuts' separating the three corner sectors from the main triangle body.
Animation step 4: The three separated angle sectors float and rotate to align adjacent to each other.
Animation step 5: The three angles snap together to form a straight horizontal line. Label '180°' appears below.

sections.title: Sec 2: The Parallel Line Bridge (Prerequisite Setup)
lecture_lines: Draw a line through the top.
This line is parallel to the base.
They allow us to move angles.
animations: Animation step 1: Draw a horizontal line through the top vertex (A) of the triangle.
Animation step 2: Add parallel arrows to the new line and the base (BC) to indicate they are parallel.
Animation step 3: Highlight the angle between the left side (AB) and the new line. Flash it to show equality with angle B.
Animation step 4: Highlight the angle between the right side (AC) and the new line. Flash it to show equality with angle C.
Animation step 5: Label the newly highlighted angles as 'Alternate Interior Angles' with a subtle Z-path trace.

sections.title: Sec 3: The Transformation: Moving the Angles
lecture_lines: It fits perfectly at the top.
Now move the right angle up.
It fits on the other side.
All three sit on one line.
animations: Animation step 1: The Red angle (A) remains static at the top. The Blue angle (B) slides up along the left side (AB) to the top vertex.
Animation step 2: The Blue angle rotates into position to the left of the Red angle on the parallel line.
Animation step 3: The Green angle (C) slides up along the right side (AC) to the top vertex.
Animation step 4: The Green angle rotates into position to the right of the Red angle on the parallel line.
Animation step 5: The three angles (Blue, Red, Green) align perfectly on the straight parallel line, forming a continuous 180-degree angle.

sections.title: Sec 4: The Conclusion: A Straight Line is 180°
lecture_lines: The angles form a straight line.
animations: Animation step 1: The three individual angle sectors merge into a single glowing rectangular bar spanning the width of the parallel line.
Animation step 2: The bar pulses with a bright white light, emphasizing the total sum.
Animation step 3: Text 'Sum = 180°' appears below the bar in bold yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Sec 5: Real-World Application: The Bridge Builder
animations: Animation step 1: Fade in a simple triangular truss structure. Highlight the central triangle.
Animation step 2: Label the bottom-left angle '60°' in Red (#FF5733).
Animation step 3: Label the bottom-right angle '70°' in Blue (#33A1FF).
Animation step 4: The top angle pulses. A calculation box appears: '180 - 60 - 70 = 50°'.
Animation step 5: The top angle fills with Green (#33FF57) and is labeled '50°'. The bridge structure stabilizes with a slight bounce.
